name: Kurta
description: A versatile long top worn by both men and women. Ranges from casual cotton daily wear to heavily embroidered formal pieces.
notes: Length typically falls between hip and knee. Slit on sides from hip down is standard.

name: Blouse (Saree)
description: The fitted upper garment worn with a saree. Highly customisable — back design, neckline, sleeve style are all variable.
notes: Typically 15–18 cm below bust. Blouse back length and hook count are tailor-critical measurements.

name: Ghagra / Lehenga
description: A full, flared skirt paired with a blouse and dupatta. Grand volume and heavy embellishment make it a staple for weddings and festivals.
notes: Flare is determined by the number of panels (kalis). Standard is 8–16 panels. Waist band is critical.

name: Daily Wear Dress
description: Simple, comfortable dresses for everyday use — A-line cuts, straight cuts, or wrap styles in breathable fabrics.
notes: Ease allowance of 3–5 cm is recommended for comfort. Avoid structured interfacing for casual wear.

name: Anarkali Suit
description: A long, flowing flared kurta with fitted bodice and flared skirt silhouette, paired with churidar or palazzo pants.
notes: Floor-length Anarkalis need accurate heel height to determine final hem. Flare starts at the waist or empire line.

name: Salwar Kameez
description: A three-piece set: kameez (top), salwar (trouser), and dupatta. One of the most common daily and semi-formal outfits.
notes: Salwar crotch depth and kameez length relative to hip are the two most critical tailoring points.
